chunks: Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Isa al-Alawi, who said: My father, Isa ibn Muhammad, narrated to me from his father, Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Ja'far, from his father, Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said to me:

He said to me: 'O my son, when the fifth descendant of the seventh of the Imams is lost, then by Allah, by Allah, be cautious about your faith, for there must be an occultation for the Master of this Command, during which many who believed in this matter will turn away from it. O my son, it is merely a trial from Allah by which He tests His creation. If your fathers and grandfathers had known a creed more sound than this creed, they would have followed it.' Abu al-Hasan said: 'So I said to him: O my master, who is the fifth descendant of the seventh?' He said: 'O my son, your intellects are too small to comprehend this and your dreams are too narrow to bear it, but if you live, you will attain it.'

key_terms.صَاحِبِ الْأَمْرِ: the Master of the Command (referring to the Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: Who is the fifth descendant of the seventh Imam and what is the significance of his occultation?
ai.summary: In this tradition from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam Musa ibn Ja'far (AS) identifies the fifth descendant of the seventh Imam as the Mahdi, whose occultation serves as a divine trial (*fitnah*) to test the steadfastness of the faithful. He emphasizes that while the specific identity remains veiled from full human comprehension, it is a predetermined reality that will be realized by those who survive to witness it, underscoring the continuity of the Imamate through the line of the Twelve Imams.
